records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
Master's students on a J-1 can do Academic Training (AT) for up to **18 months, or the length of their degree program, whichever is shorter**. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension. ([ISSS Academic Training page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment))

Key conditions:
- AT done during your studies and after your program ends are added together, and full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- The training must be directly related to the major field of study on your DS-2019.
- AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date, and it must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- Submit your request to ISSS at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends allowing about three weeks, since review takes roughly 4-5 business days. The form is on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).

**Rule change to be aware of:** DHS published a final rule on July 17, 2026 that would eliminate "duration of status" and would require an extension from USCIS for post-completion training. On September 14, 2026, a federal court postponed its effective date and barred DHS from implementing it ([ISSS announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status)). ISSS is monitoring the situation.

I can't give advice on your individual status, so please confirm your exact AT time and any STEM extension with an ISSS advisor.
